subject: literature
passage: Captain Ferris spoke of his voyages so often, and with such scrupulous modesty, that his listeners came gradually to understand how heroic they had been. He never claimed to have saved the ship in the great gale of 1858; he merely mentioned, in passing, that the rest of the crew had been below and that he had happened to remain at the wheel for nineteen hours. It was a manner of narration that disclaimed every merit while ______ each one, and the captain was, I believe, sincerely astonished that anyone could find it tiresome.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The captain never states his heroism directly; he only mentions details "in passing" that lead listeners to see it. "While" sets up a contrast with "disclaimed every merit," so the blank must mean "suggesting indirectly."
explanation.A: Incorrect. He clearly remembers every detail of his merits, since he keeps mentioning them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The captain does not overstate anything; he understates, and the details themselves reveal his heroism. The text gives no sign that the nineteen hours are untrue.
explanation.C: Correct. "Insinuating" means hinting at something indirectly, which fits a man who denies his merits while dropping details that make them obvious.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Renouncing" means giving up or rejecting, which repeats "disclaimed" instead of contrasting with it.
